## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet, and scores stay hidden, so these proposals rest on what the task requires. To place an exact brick, the agent must find where a footprint would land (the maximum build height under it) and check that the target is missing exactly those cells at that layer, with nothing extra. The starting head only sees max, min and mean pools of a projection, so it may not join information across cells well. The 5x5 receptive field and the lack of global context may also limit ordering and DONE decisions. The budget is small (131k steps), so using fewer PPO epochs to get more fresh samples may help. A higher gamma and lambda let the exact-build bonus reach earlier steps. Each candidate tests a separate axis: the recipe alone, the head plus recipe, and a deeper trunk with global context plus recipe.

### Round 2
Scores are hidden, so I only know that all three round-1 trials trained without errors. None of them can be ranked. Round 2 should therefore combine the ideas with the strongest prior reasons and stay varied. The task comes down to finding the brick whose landing layer, which is the highest built cell under its footprint, equals the layer where every covered cell is a missing target cell, without sealing missing cells underneath. The starting network merges all layers into one set of channels per column at the first 1x1 conv, so it has to learn layer-wise comparisons indirectly. I propose three candidates, all on the sample-rich recipe (2 epochs, 128 envs, gamma 0.97, lambda 0.95):
1. A per-layer branch with shared weights and footprint convs, gated across layers. This is new.
2. The footprint-window head on the sample-rich recipe, which combines r1c1 and r1c2.
3. Attention across all cells for whole-grid ordering, plus the window head. This is new.

### Round 3
No scores are visible, so I can only go on whether trials ran and on design reasoning. All six trials trained without errors and stayed well inside the time limit at r ≤ 1.8. The ideas tried so far are: a sample-rich recipe (2 epochs, gamma 0.97), a head with one conv per brick footprint ("window head"), a deeper trunk with a global broadcast, a per-layer scorer with a landing-layer gate, and attention. I have no evidence on which of these is best. The best bet is to combine the parts most likely to help on their own and to push the most plausible lever, which is sample count at a fixed budget, further. Each candidate changes one main thing relative to r2c2 (window head with 2 epochs) or r2c1 (per-layer scorer), so the final selection has a good chance of including a strong configuration.

### Round 4
Scores are hidden, so the choice rests on task structure. The footprint-window head (r1c2/r2c2/r3c1) scores each placement from the exact covered cells, which looks like the most fitting design. Recipes with fewer epochs trade data reuse for more fresh designs (307k steps with 1 epoch) and stay inside the time limit. A brick lands on the highest filled cell under its footprint, which needs a max over the covered cells. A linear window conv plus one ReLU computes this poorly, while max/min pooling gives it directly. So a head combining the window conv with pooling is the most promising refinement. For this last round I give the combined head two recipes (2 epochs, and 1 epoch with the legal-action mask as input). The third candidate keeps r3c1's network and tests a longer horizon with lower entropy for sharper greedy play.
